card.name: Bardo Chham
card.tagline: Masked dance of good versus evil zodiac animals
card.profile: Bardo Chham is a folk dance of the Sherdukpen (and Monpa) Buddhist communities of West Kameng, Arunachal Pradesh, rooted in Tibetan Buddhism - 'Bardo' is the intermediate state between death and rebirth and 'Chham' means dance (Wikipedia). Based on the triumph of good over evil, the dance holds that twelve evil forces appear as animals through the year; performers don colourful wooden animal masks representing the zodiac and dance to a large frame drum and cymbals to fight these forces. It is interpreted locally as 'dance of the zodiac' and performed by both men and women on festive occasions (History of Monyul; Gosahin).
card.insight: The dance survives through oral transmission within the small Sherdukpen tribe, with no formal training schools, making it a fragile vehicle of the community's cosmology and Buddhist moral teaching (DanceAsk; Saralstudy).
